title: Business Credit Score: Ranges, What’s Good & How It’s Used
summary: Understand business credit score ranges, PAYDEX, Experian and Equifax models, lender uses and the 2026 SBA 7(a) Small loan screening change.
body_markdown:
Updated November 26, 2026.


Photo:[Towfiqu barbhuiya / Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/photos/person-in-black-suit-jacket-holding-white-tablet-computer-nApaSgkzaxg) .


A **business credit score** helps lenders and trading partners assess a company’s payment performance or credit risk. There is more than one model, and the numbers use different scales. Start by identifying the bureau and model before deciding whether a score is good.


This guide gives each bureau's range in its own words, explains what "good" means on each, and shows who uses the scores, including a 2026 change at the SBA that many older guides don't reflect.


[1–100 PAYDEX score range Past payment performance](https://www.dnb.com/en-us/smb/resources/credit-scores/what-is-paydex-score.html)[1–100 Experian small-business scale Model version matters](https://www.experian.com/small-business/business-credit-score)


## Business Credit Score Ranges: What's Good on Each Scale


So **what is a good business credit score** ? It depends on whose score it is. Each bureau builds its own model from the payment data it collects, so the same company can look strong on one report and thin on another. The **business credit score range** for each major model is below.


### Dun & Bradstreet PAYDEX


The **PAYDEX score** runs from 1 to 100 and measures one thing: how promptly you pay vendors, weighted by dollar amount.[Dun & Bradstreet's bands](https://www.dnb.com/en-us/smb/resources/credit-scores/db-credit-scores-ratings.html) are 80 to 100 for low risk of late payment, 50 to 79 for moderate risk and 0 to 49 for high risk. On[D&B's PAYDEX key](https://www.dnb.com/content/dam/web/smb/credit/content/what-is-the-paydex-score/DnB_Paydex_Score_Infographic.pdf) , a score of 80 means you pay on terms, higher scores mean you pay early, and a 70 means you pay about 15 days late.


To have a PAYDEX at all, a company needs a D-U-N-S Number, which is[free to request](https://www.dnb.com/en-us/smb/duns/get-a-duns.html) , and at least three trade experiences reported by at least two vendors, according to a[D&B sample report](https://www.dnb.com/content/dam/web/risk/finance/content/finance-analytics-sample-report/DnB_Finance-Analytics-Sample-Credit-Report.pdf) .


### Experian Intelliscore Plus


On small-business reports,[Experian's Intelliscore Plus](https://www.experian.com/small-business/business-credit-score) also runs from 1 to 100, but it predicts serious delinquency instead of scoring past payments alone.[Experian's bands](https://smallbusiness.experian.com/pdp.aspx?pg=Glossary) are 76 to 100 low risk, 51 to 75 low to medium, 26 to 50 medium, 11 to 25 medium to high and 1 to 10 high risk. It draws on payment history, balances, credit use, public records, years on file, industry and company size. Lenders may see[a newer version](https://www.experian.com/content/dam/marketing/na/assets/bis/business-information/brochures/intelliscore-plus-v3-ps.pdf) of the score on a 300 to 850 scale.


### Equifax Business Scores


Equifax’s[Business Credit Industry Report Plus 2.0 guide](https://assets.equifax.com/marketing/US/assets/efx-2036_bcir_plus_2-0.pdf) shows a Payment Index alongside OneScore for Commercial. The Payment Index runs from zero to 100; 90 or above means paid as agreed. Interpret OneScore using the model information supplied with your report. Older samples use different risk and failure-score scales, which should not be substituted for the model you actually receive.


### FICO SBSS


The FICO Small Business Scoring Service score[ranges from 0 to 300](https://www.myfico.com/credit-education/blog/personal-credit-impact-business-financing) and is used by many small-business lenders, according to FICO. The SBA also used it to screen 7(a) small loan applications, which is no longer true (see below).


### Business credit score: read the model before the number


**PAYDEX**


A dollar-weighted record of payment performance. On-terms payment corresponds to 80.


**Experian Intelliscore Plus**


The small-business report uses a 1–100 scale. Confirm the version before applying a cutoff.


**Equifax**


Read the Payment Index and OneScore separately. They describe different aspects of risk.


Sources:[Dun & Bradstreet](https://www.dnb.com/en-us/smb/resources/credit-scores/what-is-paydex-score.html) ,[Experian](https://www.experian.com/small-business/business-credit-score) and[Equifax](https://assets.equifax.com/marketing/US/assets/efx-2036_bcir_plus_2-0.pdf) .


## How a Business Credit Score Is Used


[Dun & Bradstreet lists](https://www.dnb.com/en-us/smb/resources/credit-scores/what-is-paydex-score.html) five groups that may check a **PAYDEX score** : lenders, vendors, customers, landlords and insurance companies. They use them to decide whether to do business with you, to set credit terms and to set insurance premiums.


- **Lenders** use the score alongside cash flow and collateral to approve credit and price it.
- **Vendors** use it when deciding whether to offer payment terms such as net 30, and how large a credit limit to give.
- **Insurers** may use business credit data in pricing. The SBA notes that[poor credit history can affect insurance rates](https://www.sba.gov/business-guide/plan-your-business/establish-business-credit) .
- **Landlords and customers** may check it before signing a lease or a large contract.


Experian says commercial business reports can be purchased without the company’s permission. Reports about a company and consumer reports about an owner have different legal treatment. The[FTC’s 1998 staff opinion](https://www.ftc.gov/legal-library/browse/advisory-opinions/advisory-opinion-haner-08-27-98) addresses commercial reports; it should not be read as removing protections from every report containing personal consumer information. Review errors with the relevant bureau.


## What Changed for SBA 7(a) Small Loans


SBA’s[Procedural Notice 5000-876777](https://legacy.sba.gov/document/procedural-notice-5000-876777-sunset-sbss-score-supplemental-guidance) ended its SBSS screening requirement for 7(a) Small loans effective March 1, 2026. This change does not retire the FICO model or stop other lenders from using it.


The notice requires lender credit analysis for 7(a) Small loans. It specifies debt service coverage of at least 1.10 to one on a historical or projected basis, under its calculation rules, and says an internal scoring model cannot rely solely on consumer credit scores. Confirm the current requirements with your participating lender. Our[SBA 7(a) guide](https://www.dripcapital.com/en-us/resources/finance-guides/sba-7-a-loan) explains the broader program.

## Business vs. Personal Credit Score


A personal FICO score runs from 300 to 850 and is tied to your Social Security number. A **business credit score** is tied to the company, not to you. Dun & Bradstreet files it under the company's D-U-N-S Number, and Experian and Equifax use their own business ID numbers. Several of the scales run only to 100.

A lender may consider both the company and its owners, especially when the business has a limited credit history. Ask which reports it will review and what supporting financial records it needs. Our[equipment financing guide](https://www.dripcapital.com/en-us/resources/blog/how-equipment-financing-works) shows how credit fits alongside asset and cash-flow analysis.


## What Moves a Business Credit Score


The bureaus weigh different things, but the same handful of inputs show up across their pages:


- **Payment history.** This is the whole of PAYDEX and a factor in the others, so paying on or before terms is the most direct lever.
- **Credit use.** How much of your available credit you are using, and the trend.
- **Public records.** Liens, judgments and bankruptcies.
- **Age, size and industry.** Years on file, company size and the risk of your sector.


Negative items don't last forever. On[Experian business reports](https://www.experian.com/small-business/how-long-credit-report) , trade data stays for 36 months, judgments, tax liens and collections for six years and nine months, and bankruptcies for nine years and nine months. PAYDEX uses trade experiences reported in the last 24 months.


For the step-by-step process, from getting an EIN to opening vendor accounts that report, see our guide on[how to build business credit](https://www.dripcapital.com/en-us/resources/blog/how-to-build-business-credit) .


## How to Check Your Business Credit Score


Some providers offer free credit-profile summaries or alerts; full numeric scores and reports depend on the product and tier. Compare what is included before subscribing. The following D&B and Experian prices were checked on November 26, 2026; verify the checkout terms before paying.


Provider Access options Published price


Dun & Bradstreet[Credit Insights: Free / Basic / Plus / Premium](https://www.dnb.com/en-us/products/dnb-credit-insights.html) $0 / $49 / $149 / $199 per month


Experian[CreditScore / ProfilePlus / Business Credit Advantage](https://smallbusiness.experian.com/pdp.aspx?pg=products-and-pricing&link=5500) $59.95 one-time / $69.95 one-time / $199 per year


Equifax[Business credit report through its reseller](https://www.equifax.com/business/product/business-credit-reports-small-business/) Check the current report and price before ordering


Check all three at least once. A vendor may report to one bureau and not the others, so a clean file at one doesn't mean a complete file everywhere. Look for accounts that aren't yours, payments marked late that were on time, and outdated company details.


### Business credit score: which report should you check?


**Applying for financing**


Ask the lender which bureau and model it uses, and whether it reviews owner credit too.


**Seeking vendor terms**


Ask which report the vendor checks. Confirm that your payment history is being reported.


**Building a PAYDEX file**


D&B requires a D-U-N-S Number and at least three trade experiences from at least two vendors, subject to its review.


Source for PAYDEX requirements:[D&B sample report](https://www.dnb.com/content/dam/web/risk/finance/content/finance-analytics-sample-report/DnB_Finance-Analytics-Sample-Credit-Report.pdf) .

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is a good business credit score?


On Dun & Bradstreet's PAYDEX, 80 to 100 is the low-risk band and 80 means you pay vendors on terms. On Experian's Intelliscore Plus, 76 to 100 is low risk. On Equifax's Payment Index, 90 or above means bills were paid as agreed. Each bureau uses its own scale, so always check which score a lender or vendor is quoting.


### Is a 76 Dun and Bradstreet score good?


A PAYDEX of 76 sits in Dun & Bradstreet's moderate-risk band, which covers 50 to 79. It suggests you pay vendors a little after the due date on average. An 80 means you pay on terms and puts you in the low-risk band. PAYDEX is weighted by dollar amount, so paying your largest invoices on time has the most effect.


### Does an LLC have its own credit score?


An LLC can have its own business credit file. A newly formed LLC may have a thin file or no score; a model needs enough qualifying information to calculate one. Reporting and minimum-data requirements differ by bureau.


### What credit score do you need for an SBA loan?


For 7(a) Small loans, SBA ended its SBSS screening requirement effective March 1, 2026. Lenders still review credit and repayment ability under applicable SBA rules and their own underwriting. Ask the lender which model and requirements apply to your application.


### How do I check my business credit score for free?


D&B Credit Insights offers a free tier for an overview of business credit health. Check which numeric scores, reports and alerts are included in your selected tier. Some financial institutions also provide score access to their customers.


### Can anyone see my business credit score?


Commercial business reports can be purchased by other businesses and creditors. Consumer reports about an owner are subject to different access rules. Check the report type and dispute inaccurate information with the bureau.


### How long do negative items stay on a business credit report?


It varies by bureau. On Experian business reports, trade payment data stays for 36 months, judgments, tax liens and collections for six years and nine months, and bankruptcies for nine years and nine months. Dun & Bradstreet's PAYDEX uses trade experiences reported in the last 24 months, so older late payments eventually drop out of the score.
